nodes.label: card-face.svg (shipped card front)
nodes.rationale: The shipped front of the membership card, served as a static asset and loaded through by MembershipCard.tsx. It is the design export itself, not a CSS reconstruction: identical viewBox, identical Figma export symbol ids (clip0_42_1891, mask1_42_1891, mask2_42_1891, paint0_linear_42_1891, image0_42_1891, image1_42_1891) and identical path geometry. Exactly two edits versus the source: the 26 outlined specimen glyph paths were deleted, and mask0_42_1891 with its two full-bleed white rectangles was deleted so the rounded corners stay transparent instead of showing white.

nodes.label: Ship the Export, Overlay the Live Text
nodes.source_location: diff vs design export: 26 glyph paths + mask0_42_1891 removed
nodes.rationale: The design file is shipped as the artwork and only the two fields that differ per member are re-added as live HTML text, positioned in the artwork's own 540x340 coordinate space at the coordinates the removed glyphs occupied (1cqw = 5.4 units, so registration holds at any rendered size). The alternative — rebuilding the face in CSS — could never work, because the wordmark is a licensed narrow serif that ships no webfont, so live text fell through to a stand-in stack and lost the HOTEL & RESIDENCE line, and the line art had to be hand-scaled into a box that never quite matched. Both edits are recorded so a re-export can be repeated. The white full-bleed rectangle had to go too: the export hides it under the gradient, but it showed at the rounded corners.

nodes.label: Charcoal Card Gradient
nodes.rationale: The card's ground: a 48-stop linear ramp from #221C1B to #4A4240 running along (0.077, 0.053) to (306.696, 486.629) over a 540x340 face — about 147.8deg in CSS terms — and holding the darkest value flat for roughly the first tenth before it opens up. Both faces of the card declare the identical ramp; the back re-expresses the same values as rgb percentages under a 0.749 gradientTransform. It shows through at the transparent corners and in the moment before the artwork loads, so the CSS variable that stands in for it is derived from these exact numbers rather than approximated — a 135deg guess reads as a visible seam against the artwork.
